---
title: "Normal Distribution of IQ"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(sd, sigma)

perc <- function(p) {
  sprintf("%.1f%%", p*100)
}

task <- "llnorm3"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))

hook(perc(.X), "100%" * .X)
# hook(perc(.X), .X*100L)

## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  sd <- 15
  mu <- 100
  Q <- quote(search(llnorm3, llnorm3(mu, sd), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(
  t$correct, t$explanations, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra
)
```

Question
========

In ICD-11, a mild disorder in intelligence development (6A00.0) is quantified with an IQ 
(normally distributed with $\mu$ = 100, $\sigma$ = 15) between two and three standard deviations below the mean. 
What proportion of the population falls within this range? 

```{r questionlist, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The proportion is calculated by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
